articles.title: Major stock market rallies, do they continue today?
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
Jensen Huang is being brought back.
 At least by Nvidia’s board,
 following pressure from President Trump.
 According to Bloomberg,
 the decision was made at breakneck speed,
 without consulting any parts of the executive leadership other than the board.
 Huang is now returning after 10 days,
 prompting news agencies to dust off the old "too big to fail" concept—though this time applied to a CEO.
 Government sources say the move was made in the best interest of shareholders,
 employees,
 partners,
 and customers.
 The news sent Nvidia’s stock rebounding by 31% (!
),
 after having lost 50% since October 6,
 though it remains down a net 31% from its peak.
After a couple of turbulent weeks,
 the event caused global stock markets to completely reverse direction.
 The S&P 500 rose 4.
7%,
 the Nasdaq 6.
5%,
 and Sweden’s OMXSPI 2.
5%.
 The momentum is rippling through the trading system,
 with Japan’s Nikkei up 4% this morning and the tech-heavy Korean KOSPI up 7%.
 Stock futures are pointing toward slight gains today.
 Ten-year government bond yields have edged down slightly,
 while two-year yields are largely unchanged or up just a basis point or two.
 The US dollar strengthened and is now trading at 1.
09,
 a level not seen since the most turbulent days around "Liberation Day.
" Crude oil prices have also worked their way down below USD 90 per barrel,
 the lowest level since late August.
Today’s economic calendar partially picks up where yesterday’s PMIs left off,
 with further survey data on future confidence.
 In Germany,
 the major Ifo survey is due out,
 alongside consumer confidence in the US.
 Yesterday’s PMI surveys painted a mixed picture across Europe,
 with continued weakness in France offset by both the manufacturing and service sectors in Germany taking an increasingly positive view of the near future.
Nordic key stories
In
Sweden 360
 (biweekly),
 the
 financial focus 
is on expectations of a lower supply of nominal bonds when the Swedish National Debt Office  (SNDO) releases its new borrowing report on Thursday.
 Regarding the SEK,
 it is simply noted that recent stock market jitters are weighing heavily on the currency.
 We are also kicking off this year’s review of the krona’s December performance.
 Historically,
PPM flows
 have weakened the SEK,
 though this pattern has been less clear in recent years.
 On the contrary,
 the krona has tended to strengthen ahead of these flows.
Today's 
political focus 
is on the Speaker’s rounds of talks (starting at 9:
30 AM) ahead of a potential third prime ministerial vote.
 The outcome is as hard to predict as the sense is strong that the climate of cooperation on the red-green side has taken a hit in recent days.
 The Centre Party is now also announcing that the uncertainty has prompted them to leave the door slightly ajar to what current prime minister Kristersson has to offer.
 This morning,
 SvD/Demoskop presented a new opinion poll (paywalled link here) in which the Moderate Party (M) reaches its highest level in over ten years.
 This aligns with other recent polls; public opinion regarding the weeks following the election has primarily benefited M.
 The Liberals (L) are below the 4% parliamentary threshold,
 and both the Christian Democrats (KD) and the Sweden Democrats (SD) are polling lower than in the general election.
 The Social Democrats (S) are losing support in this survey,
 though not as sharply as in the latest Novus poll,
 for instance,
 where M became the largest party.

articles.title: Stora börsuppgångar, fortsätter de idag?
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Jensen Huang tas tillbaka.
 I alla fall av Nvidias styrelse, efter påtryckningar från president Trump. Det förefaller enligt Bloomberg ha gått i rasande takt, utan att stämmas av med andra delar av företagsledningen än styrelsen. Huang är nu tillbaka efter 10 dagar, något som får nyhetsbyråer att damma av det gamla begreppet ”too-Big-to-Fail” men nu om en VD. Från regeringshåll sägs det ha varit utifrån aktieägarnas, anställdas, partners och kunders bästa intresse. Nyheten fick Nvidia-aktien att studsa upp 31%(!), efter att ha tappat 50% sedan 6 oktober, men den ligger fortfarande netto 31% ner från toppen.
Efter ett par turbulenta veckor fick händelsen att totalt ändra riktning på världens börser. S&P 500 steg med 4,7%, Nasdaq 6,5% och svenska OMXSPI 2,5%. Utvecklingen sprider sig genom handelssystemet och japanska Nikkei är nu på morgonen upp 4% och tekniktunga koreanska KOSPI ligger på +7%. Börsterminer pekar på svag uppgång idag. Tioåriga statsobligationsräntor har fallit något medan de tvååriga är i stort sett oförändrade eller upp någon enstaka räntepunkt. US-dollarn stärktes och ligger nu på 1,09, en nivå vi inte sett sedan de mest turbulenta dagarna kring ”Liberation Day”. Råoljepriset har nu också letat sig ner under 90 USD per fat, den lägsta nivån sedan slutet av augusti.
Dagens datakalender
 tar delvis vid efter gårdagens PMI med fler enkätundersökningar om tillförsikten framöver. I Tyskland kommer stora ifo-undersökningen och i USA konsumentförtroendet. Gårdagens PMI-undersökningar gav en blandad bild över Europa med fortsatt svagt läge i Frankrike som balanseras av att både industri och tjänstenäringar i Tyskland ser alltmer positivt på den närmaste framtiden.
Sverige
I 
Sweden 360
(varannan vecka) ligger det 
finansiella fokuset
 på förväntan om lägre utbud av nominella obligationer när Riksgälden släpper sin nya upplåningsrapport på torsdag. För kronan konstateras helt enkelt att börsfrossan den senaste tiden väger tungt på valutan. Vi drar också igång årets genomgång av kronans decemberutveckling. Historiskt har PPM -flödena försvagat kronan, men de senaste åren har det inte varit lika tydligt. I motsats har kronan snarare haft tendens att stärkas inför flödena.
Det 
politiska fokuset
 idag ligger på talmansrundorna (med start 09.30) inför en eventuell tredje statsministeromröstning. Utgången är lika svår att förutse som känslan är stark att samarbetsklimatet de senaste dagarna fått sig en törn på den rödgröna sidan. Nu meddelar också Centerpartiet att oklarheten gör att man gläntar på dörren till vad Kristersson har att erbjuda. Nu på morgonen presenterar SvD/Demoskop en ny opinionsundersökning (betallänk 
här
) där M når sin högsta nivå på över tio år. Det är i samma riktning som andra undersökningar den senaste tiden; opinionens dom av veckorna efter valet har primärt gynnat M. L ligger under 4%-spärren och både KD och SD har lägre procenttal än vid Riksdagsvalet. S tappar i denna undersökning stöd, men inte så mycket som i t ex senaste Novus där M blev största parti

articles.title: Risk-off move put SEK under pressure
articles.heading: Sweden 360
articles.fulltext:
Sweden 360 provides you with a quick and broad overview of Swedish macro, rates and FX.
*** See attachment for full report ***
Macro highlight: Riksbank – December rate hike unlikely
Riksbank hearing in Parliament:
 The overall tone was relatively balanced, suggesting further, gradual tightening. 
All Board members seem reluctant to provide firm guidance. Gov. Thedéen noted that rates “might need to rise once or a few more times, but it’s very uncertain”.
Economic activity was described as strong, although all members acknowledged the challenges facing households and businesses from higher energy prices and interest rates. The labour market assessment was nuanced.
Downplaying low inflation.
 The Board has seemed reluctant to attach much significance to low inflation, with none commenting directly on the large downside surprise in October.
December hike unlikely.
 Neither the hearing nor other communication since the November decision suggest that a rate hike in December is probable. 
Markets are pricing ~20% probability of a December hike and a full hike by March. While a Dec hike looks unlikely, we view pricing as broadly fair. However, market pricing indicate a high probability of two additional hikes, which we find too aggressive – look for opportunity to fade.
Rates highlights: 
NDO forecast – slightly lower nominal bond issuance in 2027
We predict that NDO will lower nominal bond issuance slightly in 2027
, compared to the plans from May, and reduce the number of weekly auctions to 45 from 48. This would bring total issuance to 225bn in 2027. 
Read more in our Preview:
SEB Research.
The central government budget balance has been SEK 40bn higher than the NDO’s May forecast. A one-off payment from the EU explains the stronger finances and both 
tax revenues and government expenditure have been broadly as expected
. 
According to the NDO’s May forecast, the budget balance will deteriorate significantly over the next 6 months. 
Stronger growth 
than the NDO projected implies that the underlying budget balance will be revised slightly higher. We expect the NDO’s 2026 GDP forecast will be revised 1pp higher. NDO will add 2028 to the forecast; the medium-term forecast will be important for issuance plans.
The outlook for fiscal policy is uncertain 
– budget rules imply tighter fiscal policy ahead, but messy government negotiations means that outlook is uncertain. 
Increased military spending and support for Ukraine will continue to exert downward pressure on the budget balance. Support to Ukraine has been delayed but seem to be largely in line with the NDO’s forecast.
The Riksbank will most likely request that the NDO borrows SEK200bn in foreign currency
 for re-lending as a hedge for the Riksbank’s currency reserve. The NDO will wait for a formal request before including this borrowing in the forecast but will probably 
discuss the implications in the report.
FX highlights I: Positioning reduction done – SEK sensitive to risk beta amid AI jitters  
‘Easy’ positioning correction over and done in EUR/SEK
. The potential for SEK short covering has played out and markets have turned their attention to the sell-off in equities, with risk-off weighing heavily on SEK. While positioning once again has turned clearly short SEK, CHF is likely to be the better trade among carry funders in general risk off environment.
FX highlights II: SEK with December seasonality but not in the beginning of the month
Less clear seasonal impact in the beginning of December. 
Historically, EUR/SEK tended to head higher early Dec in anticipation of the yearly premium pension dispersion – ”PPM-flows”. 
A large part of what is distributed was typically invested abroad and has therefore led to SEK outflows and a weaker SEK. T
he impact has faded in recent years as a large part of 
new payouts have been used to restore the fixed income allocation balance (mainly in SEK) in 
the default premium pension fund 
AP7 
Såfa
. 
However, since 2025, AP7 rebalances assets several times during the year, rather than once in Dec – potentially opening for a negative impact on the SEK if a larger share of payments are allocated in foreign equities. In any event, we do not expect any notable impact.
EUR/SEK still tends to fall in December as a whole. 
This is true versus EUR, USD as well as NOK:
EUR/SEK:
- Has fallen in Dec 12 out of the past 15 years by an average of -0.7%. 
- Has fallen 3 years in a row and by 1.3% in 2025.
USD/SEK:
- Has fallen in Dec 11 out of the past 15 years by an average of -1.2%.
- Fell by 2.5% in 2025.
NOK/SEK: 
- 
Has fallen in Dec 12 out of the past 15 years by an average of -0.8%.
 - 
Has fallen 2 years in a row and by 2.1% in 2025.
FX highlights III: 
NOK/SEK seasonality and resemblance to AUD/NZD turnaround
NOK/SEK turnaround. 
Seasonal patterns for NOK/SEK indicate a heightened probability for a turnaround to materialize already at the end of the year.
Should lower energy prices become more persistent, NOK would lose support from both its commodity beta and the carry-trade as market pricing on Norges Bank turns south, just as it already has done for AUD. 
The development in AUD/NZD – one carry investing currency with high-rate levels vs one carry funder with lower rate levels – where market pricing on RBA has fallen and taken AUD/NZD lower, works well as illustration of what ought to happen to NOK/SEK during 2027.
Upcoming data and events - what to watch?
Debt office report (Thu):
 We predict the NDO to lower 2027 nominal bond issuance by SEK 15bn to SEK 220bn, by reducing the number of weekly auctions to 45 from 48.
Final GDP (Fri):
 Household consumption and 
other expenditure side metrics imply that final Q3 GDP (presented November 27) will be revised higher compared to the flash estimate (0.4%, 2.8% y/y). Weak production in September is an uncertain factor, but there has been a downside bias for flash GDP vs final. We predict GDP to grow by 0.6%, 3.0% y/y (Riksbank 0.2%, 2.7% y/y). 
NIER survey (Fri): 
Business sentiment, most notably manufacturing, increased markedly in October, but consumer confidence (CCI) declined markedly indicating downside risks for household consumption during the 
autumn
 and winter. We predict CCI to decline further in November and predict business confidence will reverse parts of the strong increase in October.
Week Ahead: 
SEB Research

articles.title: NOK 2bn in NST481 and NST485
articles.heading: NGB Spotlight
articles.fulltext:
On Wednesday Nov 25th, Norges Bank will hold a multiple tap auction where a total of NOK 2bn will be issued, split between the NST481 (1.75%, 09/2029) and the NST485 (3.50%, 10/2042) bonds. NST481 currently trades with a yield of 4.525%, implying a maturity-matched spread vs. Germany of 144bps and an ASW spread of -21bps. NST485 trades with a yield of 4.12%, with corresponding spread levels at 54bps and -1bps. The auction closes at 11.00 CET, and results will be available on Norges Bank’s website at 11.05 CET. Ahead of the auction there will be a buyback auction of NST479 (1.75%, 02/2027) which closes at 10:00 CET.
On Wednesday, Norges Bank will auction a total of NOK 2bn split between NST481 (09/2029) and the NST485 (10/2042) bonds. These are the same bonds as in the previous auction which showed strong results and a high 9.7 bid-to-cover ratio in the shortest bond. Including the previous tap, NST485 has been included two times so far this year with an average bid-to-cover of 2.28 and allotment share of 35%. NST 481 has been included 7 times with an average bid-to-cover ratio of 4.83 and allotment share of 47%. Like the previous auction, we believe demand will be centered on NST481 and with the total volume capped at NOK 2bn we expect the auction to run smoothly. 
In addition, there will be a buyback auction of NST479 (02/2027). Outstanding amount before the auction (incl. government’s own holdings) is NOK 51.475bn. Short yields have rallied over the past week except for NST479 which has been trading sideways. This has led to a sharp inversion in the very front end of the yield curve. Hence, rolling into surrounding bonds from NST479 offers a negative yield pick-up. Norges Bank offered an ad-hoc buyback in conjunction with the previous auction (Nov 11) and a total of NOK 3.5bn was bought back. The auction closes at 10:00 CET, and announcement of the auction result will be released at 10:05 CET.
Market volatility has been high, with a sharp selloff in global equities last week providing support to bonds. Long Norwegian bonds have traded directional with global peers, and yields have fallen across the curve since the start of October, though most notably in the long end. Norwegian bonds have outperformed Germany in the rally, but underlying demand has been rather lackluster which is visible in the sharp underperformance against swaps. The risk-off sentiment triggered large receiving pressure in swaps throughout last week, especially in the front-end. The market now discounts only a 20% chance of another rate hike in total. Some probability of a rate cut is discounted from Sep 2027, while a full rate cut is priced from March 2028. We reiterate our forecast that the policy rate has likely peaked, and Norges Bank’s 
Q4 Inflation expectation survey
provided some support for our forecast. Our inflation forecast is higher than Norges Bank’s near-term trajectory, but we predict slightly lower core inflation in 2027.
Supply update: Following this auction, Norges Bank has issued a total of NOK 105bn YTD, while the annual borrowing interval is set at NOK 100-110bn (107-110bn in the Q4 guidance). We expect Norges Bank to issue the maximum amount, implying NOK 3bn in one of the 2 remaining auctions and NOK 2bn in the other. Looking ahead, the government’s budget proposal for 2027 showed an underlying borrowing requirement of NOK 93.6bn vs. 95.7bn in 2026. After years of under-borrowing, Norges Bank’s supply estimate has exceeded the underlying borrowing requirement over the past two years, with the aim of building up the cash reserves. We expect this to be the case also in 2027, implying a minimum of NOK 110bn in gross supply. The government’s borrowing mandate in long-term debt is increased by NOK 50bn to NOK 200bn, to provide greater flexibility and allowing for a potential increase in its own holdings. Risks to our supply estimate are thus skewed to the upside. Details will be provided in Norges Bank’s Strategy and borrowing programme due in December.

articles.title: Red warning sign – with a brave attempt at a rebound
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
One big red warning sign – key takeaways.
 The Nasdaq plunged 
10%
 during an extremely volatile week for equities, with 5.3% of the decline coming on Friday alone. The S&P 500 and Sweden’s OMXSPI ended the week down 
8.6%
 and 
5.0%
, respectively. Many AI companies are trading at stretched valuations, but frankly, the potential of AI technology is extremely difficult – if not impossible – to quantify. From an economist’s perspective, there are 
three reasons
 behind the AI sell-off: 
(1)
 signs of increasing 
political intervention in AI
, reflecting 
shifting power dynamics in Washington
 and Trump’s decision to 
penalise US companies seeking to build data centres abroad
; 
(2)
rising short- and long-term real interest rates
, forcing a more aggressive discounting of future earnings – i.e. lower equity valuations – while also raising funding costs; and 
(3) seasonal factors
, as major investors seek to 
“close their books”
 and lock in strong performance figures ahead of year-end. This increases the risk of deteriorating market liquidity, potentially amplifying price swings. Analysts – and economists – now need to distinguish between AI valuations and the long-term impact of these transformative technologies on growth, inflation and productivity. Anthropic shares, which surged 17% on their market debut on Thursday, also lost ground but remain 7% above their IPO price. The US 10-year Treasury yield fell by as much as 11 basis points on Friday to 4.95%, while movements in the dollar and oil (Brent) were relatively modest. Thursday’s Thanksgiving holiday will reduce market liquidity. Early on Monday, equity markets are attempting to rebound, with Nasdaq futures currently up 2.3% (see table below for other market quotes). 
A complicated world for central banks – reflections.
 In just over two weeks, the Fed will announce its next rate decision. At the time of writing, markets are pricing in a 94% probability of a 25-basis-point hike to 4.25%. It remains to be seen how the Fed – and other central banks – will navigate the new risk environment: high inflation and still-solid GDP prospects, now set against less supportive financial conditions (see chart below) and falling equity markets. The question is whether an equity market correction, within reasonable limits, might even be welcomed by the ECB and the Bank of Japan, both of which are also expected to raise their policy rates in December.
An extraordinary trilateral meeting with little substance – epilogue.
 Last week’s Xi-Putin-Trump meeting was a Russian PR success, but hardly a Yalta 2.0 – despite the Kremlin’s efforts. Trump continues, rather astonishingly, to 
refer to Putin as “my friend”. President Zelenskyy says: “To us, he is a murderer.”
 A sign of the times, reflecting the erosion of the rules-based international order and its replacement by an increasingly power-based one: 
on Friday, the UN Security Council failed – for the ninth consecutive time – to
 appoint a new UN Secretary-General. A weakened and increasingly marginalised António Guterres will leave the UN in six weeks. 
Conclusion:
 Geopolitical unpredictability must become a permanent parameter in economic forecasts. 
The next major geopolitical event:
the G20 summit in Florida on 14–15 December
, offering Trump an excellent photo opportunity on home turf. Putin has been invited, but his attendance remains unconfirmed. Notably, Europe will have a substantial presence this time – compared with Shenzhen.
Pro-EU Burnham faces a delicate political balancing act over “Breturn” – key takeaways.
Friday’s new agreement
 confirms that the gap between London and Brussels continues to narrow. However, just over 60% of Britons still oppose rejoining the EU. The new agreement sets out a timetable for food exports and emissions trading, as well as for implementing proposals to facilitate greater mobility for young people. Prime Minister Burnham, who has already made clear his ambition to forge even closer ties with the EU, claims that the new agreement will “boost UK GDP by up to 0.5%”. Does the EU want Britain back? Political fragmentation within the EU, against the backdrop of an emerging new world order, is increasing the bloc’s interest in bringing a major global player back into the fold as that new order takes shape. This means that the UK should by no means be regarded as the weaker party in the ongoing talks between Brussels and London.
Nordic key stories
70 days without a Swedish government – some reflections.
 “No, but no thanks” was the Left Party’s swift and clear response to the weekend’s offer from the three red-green parties. Government negotiations (S+C+MP+V) are progressing at a snail’s pace – like a snail crawling uphill on a sand-covered slope with the handbrake on. Frustration is growing among voters. A new TV4/Novus poll shows that 44% favour a snap election, while 36% oppose it. The question now is: will the Centre Party switch sides and join the right-wing “Alliance”? Keep an eye on 27 November, the deadline for parties to submit their alternative budget proposals. This could provide an opportunity to abandon – or at least amend – the caretaker budget if an alternative proposal secures support in parliament.

articles.title: Rött utropstecken – med tappert försök till uppstuds
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Ett enda stort rött utropstecken – slutsatser.
 Nasdaq föll 
10%
 under en extremt volatil börsvecka; 5,3% av fallet kom i fredags. Veckofacit för S&P 500 och Sveriges OMXSPI blev 
-8,6%
 respektive 
-5,0%
. Många AI-bolag uppvisar ansträngda värderingar, men ärligt talat: AI-teknologins potential är extremt svår – om inte omöjlig – att siffersätta. Ekonomen ser 
tre orsaker
 till AI-frossan: 
(1)
 tecken på ökad 
politisk styrning av AI
 – med 
nya maktbalanser i Washington
 och Trumps beslut att 
straffa USA-bolag som vill bygga utländska datorhallar
, 
(2)
uppgången i korta och långa realräntor
 som tvingar fram hårdare diskontering av framtida vinster – d v s lägre börser – och fördyrar investeringar, och 
(3) säsongsfaktorn
, d v s att stora placerare vill 
”stänga böckerna”
 för att kunna uppvisa bra siffror inför årsskiftet; det ökar risken för försämrad marknadslikviditet som kan förstärka kursrörelserna. Analytiker – och ekonomer – behöver nu kunna skilja mellan AI-värderingar och de transformerande teknologiernas långsiktiga effekter på tillväxt, inflation och produktivitet. Anthropic-aktien, som steg 17% vid noteringen i torsdags, tappade också men ligger fortfarande 7% över teckningskursen. USA:s 10-åriga ränta föll hela 11 räntepunkter i fredags till 4,95% medan rörelserna i dollarn och oljan (Brent) var ganska små. Thanksgiving på torsdag försämrar marknadslikviditeten. 
Tidig måndag försöker börserna rekylera uppåt; Nasdaq-terminen står just nu på +2,3% (se tabell nedan för övriga marknadsnoteringar).
Komplicerad centralbanksvärld – tankar.
 Om drygt två veckor lämnar Fed räntebesked; marknaden prisar i skrivande stund in 94% sannolikhet för en höjning med 25 räntepunkter till 4,25%. Det återstår att se hur Fed – och andra centralbanker – ska hantera den nya riskbilden: hög inflation och fortsatt goda BNP-utsikter, som nu ställs mot stramare finansiella förhållanden (se graf nedan) och sjunkande börser. Frågan är om en börskorrektion, inom rimliga gränser, också välkomnas av ECB och Bank of Japan, som likaså förväntas höja sina styrräntor i december.
Exceptionellt trilateralt möte utan substans – epilogen.
 Förra veckans Xi-Putin-Trump-möte blev en rysk bildmässig succé men inget Jalta 2.0 – trots Kremls ansträngningar. Trump fortsätter att – minst sagt magstarkt – 
kalla Putin för ”min vän”. President Zelenskyj säger: ”för oss är han en mördare”
.
 Ett tecken i tiden på den nedmonterade regelbaserade – och alltmer maktbaserade – världsordningen: 
FN:s säkerhetsråd misslyckades i fredags – för nionde gången
 i rad – med att
 utse ny FN-chef; en svag och vingklippt António Guterres lämnar FN om sex veckor. 
Slutsats:
 Geopolitisk oförutsägbarhet måste vara en permanent parameter i prognoser. 
Nästa storpolitiska händelse:
G20-mötet i Florida den 14–15 december
 som blir ett utmärkt fototillfälle för Trump på hemmaplan; Putin är inbjuden men hans närvaro är inte bekräftad. Notera att Europas närvaro då kommer att vara betydande – jämfört med Shenzhen.
EU-positiv Burnham går svår politisk balansgång i ”Breturn-frågan” – slutsatser.
Fredagens nya avtal
 bekräftar det fortsatt krympande avståndet mellan London och Bryssel. Men drygt 60% av britterna säger fortfarande nej till en återanslutning. Det nya avtalet innebär en tidsplan för livsmedelsexport och utsläppshandel samt för att genomföra förslaget om friare rörlighet för ungdomar. Premiärminister Burnham, som redan meddelat att han vill skapa ännu starkare band till EU, hävdar att det nya avtalet ”lyfter brittisk BNP med upp till 0,5%”. Vill EU ha tillbaka britterna? EU:s politiska fragmentering, i skuggan av framväxten av en ny världsordning, ökar EU:s intresse av att ”få tillbaka” en betydelsefull global spelare när den nya världen byggs. Det betyder att Storbritannien på intet sätt ska ses som en svag part i de fortsatta samtalen mellan Bryssel och London.
Sverige
70 dagar utan regering – reflektioner.
 ”Nej, men nej tack” blev Vänsterpartiets snabba och tydliga svar på helgens erbjudande från de tre rödgröna partierna. Regeringsförhandlingarna (S+C+MP+V) går trögt – som en snigel i en sandad uppförsbacke med handbromsen dragen. Frustrationen växer bland väljarna. En ny mätning från TV4/Novus visar att 44% är positiva till extraval; 36% är negativa. Frågan är nu: går Centerpartiet över till ”Alliansen”? Håll ett öga på den 27 november, sista dagen för partierna att lämna in sina budgetmotioner. Här finns en möjlighet att överge – eller åtminstone modifiera – övergångsbudgeten om ett alternativt budgetförslag får stöd i riksdagen.

articles.title: A busy week ahead
articles.heading: The Week Ahead
articles.fulltext:
US PCE inflation, flash PMIs and Nordic GDP figures are the key data releases. The EU summit and Black Friday spending will also be in focus, while Spain’s snap general election and Sweden’s government formation talks will be closely watched.  
US:
PCE inflation for October will be the most interesting data and is the only remaining data for inflation ahead of the Fed’s December meeting on 8-9 December. November PMIs will be watched for signs of whether strong economic momentum has continued into Q4. We will also get consumer confidence, durable goods orders, new home sales and advance goods trade. Markets will be closed during Thanksgiving on Thursday and Black Friday will as always be in focus for signals on US household spending momentum.
Euro area:
A busy data week. Flash PMIs, Germany’s ifo survey and consumer confidence figures will help gauge business and household sentiment. France and Spain will be the first to release November inflation figures next week. Final Q3 GDP figures for Germany and France, along with retail sales data, will provide a clearer picture of economic activity. On Thursday, the ECB will publish the account of its 28–29 October meeting. On the political front, we will be watching the EU summit on 26–27 November, the final vote on Germany’s 2027 federal budget on 27 November and Spain’s snap general election on 29 November.
Sweden:
Growth will be in focus, with final GDP figures for Q3 and the NIER survey as the main events. Residential construction, PPI, household lending, the trade balance and a borrowing report by the National Debt Office are also on the agenda. The Riksbank’s Jansson will speak on Thursday, while attempts to form a government will continue.
Norway:
Plenty of data next week, with several labour market indicators and mainland GDP being the highlights. Growth has been sluggish in H1, partly explained by temporary factors. We expect mainland GDP to rise 0.3% in Q3, in line with Norges Bank’s own forecast. Registered unemployment (Fri) is expected to remain at 2.0% (SA) while momentum in retail sales (Fri) is lacklustre.

articles.title: Anthropic lifted but not the AI trade
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
So finally, the first of the two major AI labs is public. Anthropic opened strongly yesterday, initially rising to $115, 39% above the introductory price of $83. But then fell down to $93, followed by sideways trading for the rest of the day until it finally closed at $97 or +17%. Although this is perfectly fine, it was far from the euphoria needed to inject new energy into the AI trade. Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta all fell just over 3%, and the market as a whole also closed down with the S&P 500 down -2.0% and the Nasdaq down -2.3%. The question is whether the stock market's focus is increasingly shifting from hopes for AI to a more traditional environment where what the Fed will do with interest rates becomes more important. 
In Asia
, 
 there is also continued concern about the AI trade with significant market drops this morning. Japan stands at -4.9%, Korea at -5.7%, and Taiwan at -6.6%. Ahead of the European opening, stock market futures are clearly pointing downward in both Europe and the US. Movements in the currency market have nevertheless been quite muted, with a generally somewhat weaker dollar. 
No major data on the agenda.
 We don't have any major figures on the agenda today. From Europe come, among other things, German producer prices and French business confidence. For Sweden, we get new labor market data. However, the statistics have been very volatile for more than a year, making it difficult to see any clear trends. In any case, we expect unemployment to remain unchanged at 8.6% last month. Today we are also keeping an eye on when the United Kingdom's Andy Burnham meets EU leaders in Brussels to finalize a new agreement on closer cooperation in trade and other areas. Although it is a step in the right direction, it is still a long way from the "Breturn" that some hope for. 
Nordic key stories
Price record.
 Finally,
 we note that at least parts of the Swedish art market seem to be red-hot. Hilma af Klint's painting "Ser III No. 5" from 1920 was valued by auction house Bukowskis at between SEK 5 and 8 million SEK but was sold yesterday for SEK 108 million, which meant a final price after fees of SEK 129 million. The most expensive artwork ever sold in the Nordic countries.
Have a great Friday.

articles.title: Anthropic lyfte men inte AI-traden
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Så äntligen var det första av de två stora renodlade AI-bolagen på börsen. Anthropic öppnade starkt igår och steg i inledningen till $115, 39% över introduktionskursen på $83. Men sen följde en rejäl utförslöpa ned till $93 och därefter sidledes handel resten av dagen för att till slut stänga på $97 eller +17%. Även om det naturligtvis är helt godkänt så var det långt ifrån den eufori som hade behövts för att ingjuta ny energi i AI-traden. Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon och Meta backade alla drygt 3% och börsen som helhet stängde också ned med S&P 500 på -2,0% och Nasdaq på -2,3%. Frågan är om inte börsens fokus alltmer håller på att skifta från förhoppningar om AI till en mer traditionell miljö där det blir viktigare vad Fed ska göra med räntan. 
I Asien
 är det också fortsatt oro för AI-traden med rejäla börsfall nu på morgonen. Japan står på -4,9%, Korea på -5,7% och Taiwan på -6,6%. Inför öppningen här hemma pekar börsterminerna tydligt ned i både Europa och i USA. Rörelserna på valutamarknaden har trots allt varit rätt små med en generellt lite svagare dollar. 
Lugn statistikfredag.
 Vi har inga tunga siffror på agendan idag. Från Europa kommer bland annat tyska producentpriser och franskt företagsförtroende. För svensk del får vi nya arbetsmarknadssiffror. Statistiken har dock varit mycket volatil i mer än ett år och det gör det svårt att se några tydliga trender. Vi räknar i alla fall med att arbetslösheten låg kvar oförändrad på 8,6% förra månaden. Idag håller vi också koll på när Storbritanniens Andy Burnham träffar EU-ledare i Bryssel för att slutföra ett nytt avtal om ett närmare samarbete kring handel och andra områden. Även om det är ett steg i rätt riktning är det lååångt kvar till en ”Breturn” som vissa hoppas på. 
Lästips: Är byråkrat ett framtidsyrke?
 Vi hör allt oftare om företag som planerar att ersätta anställda med AI. För många unga som idag står i begrepp att välja vad de vill jobba med är just frågan om vilka yrken som har störst chans att klara sig genom AI-revolutionen central. Kan det vara så att ett av dessa framtidsyrken faktiskt är byråkrat? Läs om varför i Veckans Tanke 
här
.
Sverige
Stundande bränslebrist?
 TT rapporterar om att det kan bli slut på bensin och diesel på mackar runt om i Sverige som en effekt av att priset går upp kraftigt när skattesatserna återställs till gamla nivåer vid månadsskiftet. Bensinen blir närmare 20% dyrare över en natt och Anna Törner på Drivkraft Sverige
 uppmanar alla att tanka i god tid. Samtidigt kan det vara värt att komma ihåg att bensinpriset sedan förra månaden faktiskt har gått ned mer än de 3 kr/liter som priset kommer att gå upp 1 december.
Prisrekord.
 Slutligen noterar vi att i alla fall delar av konstmarknaden verkar vara glödhet. Hilma af Klints målning ”Ser III No. 5” från 1920 var av Bukowskis värderad till mellan 5 och 8 miljoner kr men klubbades igår för 108 miljoner vilket innebar ett slutpris efter avgifter på 129 miljoner. Det dyraste konstverket som sålts i Norden. Wow.
Ha en bra fredag.

articles.title: Är byråkrat ett framtidsyrke?
articles.heading: Veckans tanke
articles.fulltext:
Vi hör allt oftare om företag som planerar att ersätta anställda med AI. För många unga som idag står i begrepp att välja vad de vill jobba med är just frågan om vilka yrken som har störst chans att klara sig genom AI-revolutionen central. Kan det vara så att ett av dessa framtidsyrken faktiskt är byråkrat? 
Idag är experter och ekonomer ganska oense om hur AI kommer att påverka arbetsmarknaden. Det ena lägret menar att AI kommer att konkurrera ut människor och ta över många yrken så att stora grupper blir arbetslösa. I det andra lägret menar man i stället att AI framför allt kommer att göra oss människor mer produktiva. De yrken som försvinner kommer precis som vid tidigare teknikskiften att ersättas av ännu fler jobb inom helt nya yrken som vi inte har någon aning om vilka de är idag.
Det nästan alla ändå är överens om är att utvecklingen av AI går otroligt fort. Det är nu nästan precis fyra år sedan ChatGPT lanserades publikt och förbättringarna har varit dramatiska under den relativt korta tiden. Men trots den snabba utvecklingen finns det fortfarande inga klara bevis för att AI håller på att göra stora grupper arbetslösa. Visst dyker det allt oftare upp nyheter om företag som ska ersätta anställda med AI som i nedanstående Di-artikel från i veckan. Men i makrosiffror som sysselsättning och arbetslöshet, syns ännu inga tydliga effekter.
Det kan bero på att AI-effekter är svåra att skilja ut från allt annat som påverkar arbetsmarknaden. En möjlig AI-effekt som många ändå pekar på och som kunnat observeras i flera länder är att unga verkar få allt svårare att komma in på arbetsmarknaden. I USA beskrivs situationen som ett läge av ”low hire, low fire”: inte många nyanställs, men få blir heller uppsagda. Även i Sverige visar en färsk studie från Tillväxtanalys att arbetskraftens rörlighet är låg och att det visserligen ännu inte syns någon bred strukturomvandling i ekonomin som helhet – men att det finns tydliga tecken på att unga drabbas. Bland nyutexaminerade studenter från utbildningar med hög AI-exponering har arbetsinkomsterna utvecklats betydligt sämre sedan 2023, samtidigt som en allt mindre andel anställs i de mest AI-exponerade företagen.
Inbyggda trögheter håller igen
Det finns säkert många förklaringar till varför det fortfarande inte syns några stora effekter på arbetsmarknaden från AI. En sådan skulle kunna vara att många företag visserligen redan i dag skulle kunna minska sin personalstyrka med hjälp av AI, men att inbyggda trögheter gör att det inte sker i någon större omfattning. Så länge ett företag går bra och gör fina vinster är ju alla rätt nöjda. Aktieägarna får sin avkastning, de anställda trivs och ledningen känner ingen yttre press att börja skära i kostnaderna genom att göra sig av med personal. Den typen av obekväma beslut tar man ju normalt först när det börjar gå dåligt och man tvingas att agera. Men samtidigt finns inte heller några större behov av att nyanställa, eftersom AI gör att man kan producera mer med sin befintliga personal.
Risk för ketchupeffekt
Personligen tillhör jag den grupp ekonomer som ändå tror att AI kommer att få betydande effekter på arbetsmarknaden. Resonerar man utifrån grundläggande principer är det svårt att komma runt att AI snabbt blir bättre på nästan allt. AI kommer att kunna utföra många jobb bättre och billigare än vi människor och det talar för att många kommer att konkurreras ut. Exakt vilka yrken som kommer att drabbas mest och först spekuleras det mycket i men den diskussionen är för stor att avhandla här. Mer generellt kan man dock anta att stora grupper antagligen kommer att påverkas rätt mycket och risken är om en sådan omvälvande förändring går så fort så att ekonomin och samhället inte hinner anpassa sig. Då leder det till mycket missnöje och sociala spänningar som kan bli svåra att hantera.
Men just det faktum att saker går väldigt snabbt är utmärkande för AI. Så länge AI inte är tillräckligt generell och pålitlig för att kunna göra allt det vi människor kan, så är de flesta jobb säkra. De flesta yrken innehåller många arbetsuppgifter där alla ännu inte kan tas över av en AI. Men när väl AI blir så bra att den passerar den tröskeln, ja då kan den plötsligt klara att utföra massor av yrken. Inte minst den snabba utvecklingen av AI-agenter som till skillnad från att svara på frågor i en chatt också kan agera och utföra uppgifter ger en antydan om vart vi är på väg. Risken är att vi står inför en jättelik ketchupeffekt de kommande åren. Så vad kan vi göra för att hantera ett sådant scenario?
Nyckeln till en ordnad omställning i ett sådant läge är att nya jobb skapas i en takt som ger ekonomin och människor tid att anpassa sig. Men frågan är var de jobben ska komma ifrån?
Fler byråkrater?
Politiker kommer att få en nyckelroll i att säkerställa att omställningen görs i en takt som samhället mäktar med och som en del i det är det inte osannolikt att många nya jobb kommer att skapas genom politiska beslut. Kanske är byråkrat faktiskt ett av framtidsyrkena. Ordet har idag en negativ klang, men så behöver det inte vara i framtiden. I praktiken handlar det om att vi i många fall faktiskt vill att en människa ska vara med och fatta beslut eller ta fram underlag som påverkar oss vare sig det gäller ett bygglov från kommunen eller en kreditansökan hos banken.
Det finns förstås en kostnad. Om uppgifter som tekniskt sett skulle kunna automatiseras blir dyrare och långsammare när en människa ska vara med, så måste det betalas via skatter eller högre priser än vad som annars skulle vara fallet. Men om alternativet är massarbetslöshet och växande sociala spänningar kan det vara en kostnad som ändå är väl värd att betala.
Så bli inte förvånad om antalet ”byråkrater” ökar när AI på allvar börjar ta sig in på arbetsmarknaden. Och se inte heller det som ett misslyckande utan som en del i att underlätta en anpassning till en ny tid.

articles.title: Easing business leaders’ expectations
articles.heading: Norwegian inflation expectations
articles.fulltext:
Inflation expectations were broadly unchanged in the Q4 survey, though importantly business leaders revised their CPI expectations lower. Wage growth expectations align with the wage norm in 2026, remaining somewhat below Norges Bank’s forecast in 2027. Moreover, the downward revision in social partners’ wage growth expectations should also ease the Bank’s concerns, as the group has been highlighted previously as particularly important for wage formation. To conclude, though the survey sends some comforting messages, it also confirms that long-term inflation expectations remain sticky and above target. We reiterate that we expect the policy rate to have peaked.
Details:
CPI expectations:
 On average, CPI expectations were revised marginally higher in the near-term while broadly unchanged in the medium- and long-term horizons in the Q4 2026 survey. More comforting is the downward revision of business leaders’ inflation expectations, implying CPI to average 4.0% (-0.2pp) in the next 12 months while unchanged in the 2-year horizon (4.6%). Economists have lifted their CPI expectations 0.1pp, now expecting CPI at 3.1% in the next 12 months, while expecting CPI unchanged at 2.7% in 2 years. Social partners have unchanged inflation expectations both in the near term and in the medium term, at 3.0% and 2.6%, respectively. On average long-term inflation expectations are unchanged at 2.4% and thus remain above target. 
Wage growth:
 Economists’ wage expectations in 2026 and 2027 are unchanged at 4.3% and 3.8%, respectively. Social partners increased their wage growth expectations in 2026 while expecting marginally lower wage growth in 2027, at 4.5% and 3.8% respectively. On average, wage growth expectations are thus seen at 4.4% and 3.8%, aligning with Norges Bank’s estimate this year while 0.2pp below its forecast in 2027. Though this may suggest easing concerns from second-rounds effects from previously high wage growth, survey estimates were below Norges Bank’s forecast also in the Q3 survey. Note that expected wage growth in 2026 is 0.1pp below the 4.4% wage norm for 2026. Wage growth in the 5y horizon is on average seen at 3.2%. Average real wage growth is thus broadly unchanged at 1.4% this year, 1.2% in 2027 and 0.8% in 5y.
Business profitability:
 Expected profitability has deteriorated somewhat. On average, 37.3% of business leaders expect profitability to weaken in the next 12 months, which is 7.6ppt higher than previous quarter. 25.4% of business leaders expect profitability to improve ahead (+2.5ppt) while 34.1% of business leaders expect unchanged profitability (-10.3ppt). 
Meanwhile, pricing plans are relatively stable. The share of business leaders expecting retail prices to increase less over the next 12 months increased 1.2ppt to 16.9% in Q4, while the share of business leaders that expect retail prices to increase more increased 4.4ppt to 33.5%. About 50% of business leaders expect retail prices to remain broadly unchanged in the next 12 months. 
Moreover, the survey points to some softening in employment intentions as the share of respondents saying they will likely increase the number of employees in 12 months increased 0.6ppt to 23.9%, while the share of respondents saying they will need less employees increased 3.ppt to 30.3% in Q4.
Implications Norges Bank:
 The Inflation Expectations Survey sends a somewhat comforting message in Q4 mainly due to the small relief in business leaders’ expectations. Though inflation expectations on aggregate remain elevated, there are signs that the upward pressure has abated. Moreover, the downward revision among social partners wage growth expectations is comforting, as Norges Bank previously highlighted this group as particularly important for leading wage growth. All in all, the survey underpins our expectation that the policy rate has peaked, but the road for disinflation will likely take some time and the “high for longer” approach by Norges Bank seem very reasonable.

articles.title: Anthropic's IPO beats records
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
European stock markets were mostly in the red yesterday, and pessimism persisted in the US, where the S&P 500 continued down for the fifth consecutive day after renewed declines in Nvidia. The tech-heavy Nasdaq went against the tide ahead of Anthropic's debut on the stock market. The introduction has been seen as a test of the market's continued interest in AI. It turned out that Anthropic had no trouble finding buyers. The IPO broke Spacex's previous record as the largest ever, and the company is now valued at about 1500 billion USD. Speaking of Spacex, Musk says in an interview with the New York Times that he is not MAGA, that he regrets the large sums (about 400 million USD) he invested in the Republicans ahead of the Texas election, and that he believes shared government could be good for the US. Perhaps this is the first of several outstretched hands from American tech companies now that the balance of power has shifted? In Asia, stock markets are mostly lower today, while futures are up for both the US, especially Nasdaq, and Europe.
The oil price
 has traded relatively steadily overnight at 92 USD/barrel after reports in the New York Times that President Trump is considering new attacks on Iran, along with Israel. US 10-year yields rose by some bp in connection with the release of the Fed's meeting minutes but have otherwise remained stable, and the market continues to discount just over three more hikes from the Fed. The dollar is trading below 1.10 against the euro. Weak labor market data has put pressure on AUD on expectations that the Australian central bank, RBA, is done hiking, which is also our view.
Not just Waller wanting to raise by 50 basis points. 
 The minutes from the October meeting showed that a couple of Fed members discussed the possibility of a larger hike in the event of unfavorable inflation data. Fed Governor Christopher Waller, who scared the market a few weeks ago with his 50-point hike speech, is therefore not entirely alone in this view. Otherwise, the minutes showed that most members supported the decision to keep rates unchanged in October, but that almost all expected further tightening. Data since the October meeting has been strong, and Fed members sound increasingly hawkish. We continue to believe in a hike in December, but with the possibility of another step in March 2027. Read more 
here
. Waller was interviewed yesterday by CNBC and reiterated his calls for a 50-point hike in December as a way to shock the market but also said that the Fed could settle for a 25 basis point hike if it clearly indicated a further hike in January. This is contrary to Chairman Kevin Warsh's reluctance to provide forward guidance and can be seen as yet another step in Waller's attacks against the new communication strategy.
The world's eyes today are on the APEC meeting in Shenzhen 
and the historic meeting between President Trump, Xi, and Putin. Trump and Putin have met one-on-one ahead of the tripartite meeting, and Trump will do the same with Xi later today. Trump praised the good relationship with his friend Putin but said at the same time that he would not make a deal with Putin about Ukraine without Ukraine's participation.
Today's data calendar is thin
 and topped by Norges Bank's survey of inflation expectations, labour costs, and construction in the Eurozone, as well as, in the US, the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index.
Nordic key stories
The Riksbank's executive board is being questioned
 in the Swedish Riksdag Finance Committee today. We will be watching for new clues about when the next hike will come and how Riksbank board members weigh the risk of inflation against the risk of the recovery stalling.

articles.title: Rusning efter Anthropics aktier
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Det var mestadels röda siffror på börserna i Europa igår och pessimismen höll i sig i USA där S&P500 fortsatte ned för femte dagen i rad efter förnyade nedgångar i Nvidia. Tekniktunga Nasdaq gick mot strömmen inför AI-bolaget Anthropics debut på börsen. Introduktionen har setts som ett test på marknadens fortsatta intresse för AI. Det visade sig att Anthropic inte hade några problem att hitta köpare. Emissionen slog Spacex tidigare rekord som den största någonsin och bolaget värderas nu till ca 1500 mdr USD. Apropå Spacex säger Musk, i en intervju med New York Times, att han inte är MAGA, att han ångrar de stora summor (ca 400 mln USD) som han satsade på republikanerna inför valet i Texas och att han tror att ett delat styre kan vara bra för USA. Kanske är detta den första av flera utsträckta händer från amerikanska techbolag nu när maktförhållandena har skiftat? I Asien är börserna mestadels lägre idag medan terminerna pekar uppåt för både USA, särskilt Nasdaq, och Europa.
Oljepriset
 har handlats relativt stabilt under natten på 92 USD/fatet efter rapporter i New York Times att president Trump överväger nya attacker mot Iran, tillsammans med Israel. Amerikanska 10-årsräntor steg någon punkt i samband med Feds mötesprotokoll, men har i övrigt varit stabila, och marknaden fortsätter att diskontera ytterligare drygt tre höjningar från Fed. Dollarn handlas under 1,10 mot euron. Svaga arbetsmarknadsdata satte press på AUD på förväntningar om att det är färdighöjt från den australiska centralbanken, RBA, vilket även är vår syn.
Inte bara Waller som vill höja 50 punkter. 
Protokollet från oktobermötet visade att ett par Fed-ledamöter diskuterade möjligheten till ett större höjningssteg i oktober i händelse av ogynnsamma inflationsdata. Feds guvernör Christopher Waller, som skrämde upp marknaden häromveckan med sitt tal om 50-punktershöjning, är således inte helt ensam om denna åsikt. I övrigt visade protokollet att de flesta av ledamöterna stödde beslutet om oförändrad ränta i oktober men att nästan alla förväntade sig ytterligare åtstramning. Data sedan oktobermötet har varit starka och Fed-ledamöterna låter alltmer hökaktiga. Vi fortsätter att tro på en höjning i december, men med en möjlighet till ytterligare ett steg i mars 2027. Läs mer 
här
. Waller intervjuades igår av CNBC och upprepade då kraven på en 50-punktershöjning i december som ett sätt att chocka marknaden men sa också att Fed skulle kunna nöja sig med att höja 25 punkter om man tydligt indikerade en ytterligare höjning i januari. Detta är på tvärs mot ordförande Kevin Warsh’s ovilja att ge forward guidance och kan väl ses som ännu ett led i Wallers krypskytte mot den nya kommunikationsstrategin.
Världens ögon riktas idag mot APEC-mötet i Shenzen 
och det historiska mötet mellan president Trump, Xi och Putin. Trump och Putin har träffats på tu man hand inför trepartsmötet och Trump kommer att göra detsamma med Xi senare idag. Trump hyllade den goda relationen med sin vän Putin men sa samtidigt att han inte kommer att göra upp med Putin om Ukraina utan Ukrainas medverkan.
Dagens datakalender är tunn
 och toppas av Norges Banks undersökning av inflationsförväntningar i Norge, arbetskraftskostnader och byggande i Euroområdet, samt, i USA, industriindex för Philadelphia-området.
Sverige
Riksbankens direktion frågas ut
 i Riksdagens finansutskott idag. Vi kommer att hålla utkik efter nya ledtrådar kring när nästa höjning kommer och hur direktionsledamöterna väger risken för inflation mot risken för att återhämtningen kommer av sig.

articles.title: Almost all expected a further rate increase, a couple discussed a 50 bp move
articles.heading: Fed minutes
articles.fulltext:
The minutes from the October 27-28 meeting showed that most members supported the decision to hold rates steady but that almost all expected that the Fed would raise rates further. A couple of members discussed a larger 50 bp move. Strong data since the meeting is likely to have strengthened the case for further tightening and we see it as likely that members will indicate another rate increase in their projections in December. We stick to our view of one more rate increase in December but risks are clearly skewed for another increase, possibly in March. 
Key points
Most members supported unchanged rate in October
Close call for a few members
Almost all expected the Fed to raise rates further
Waller not alone in discussing 50 bp move
We expect a rate increase in December and possibly also in March 
Unchanged rates was a close call for a few members 
The minutes from the October 27-28 meeting shows that most members supported the decision to hold rates steady, awaiting more information and (according to a couple of members) to give businesses and households time to adjust to higher interest rates. However, it was a close call for a few participants, while some favoured a rate increase. Two members, Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack, voted to raise rates by 25 bp at the October meeting and the language in the minutes suggest that their views were shared by other members. However, a few who favoured a rate increase would, according to the minutes, have supported unchanged rates provided it was “clearly understood” by market participants that further tightening was likely. This could be a sign that some members are critical against Chair Warsh’s new communication policy, including his resistance to forward guidance. Judging from his recent comments and speeches, Governor Christopher Waller is likely to be among those.
A couple saw a larger step as appropriate in case of unfavourable inflation data 
Almost all participants thought that the Fed would likely have to raise its policy rate further. The minutes also shows that the possibility of a larger 50 bp hike at the December meeting was discussed at the meeting and that “a couple” believed it could be appropriate if incoming inflation data were “unfavorable”. Thus, Governor Waller is not alone in thinking that the Fed may be forced to move in larger steps though in the minority. We also note that “some” participants thought market-implied tightening expectations were broadly consistent with their own views of an appropriate policy path. At the time of the meeting, markets were pricing a high probability for a December rate increase and two more by the summer of 2027.
Most members expected inflation to return to target over time
The minutes did otherwise not contain much news. Inflation was expected to remain elevated in the near term, but most members expected it to return to the target over time, reflecting waning effects of tariffs, a reduction in the contribution from energy and a moderation of price pressures from the AI buildout. At the same time, the “vast majority” saw upside risks to this outlook. This suggests that tighter policy could be seen as a precautionary step by the Fed rather than as necessary.
AI build-out remains in focus for the Fed
Much of the discussion focused on the risks from the AI buildout for inflation. The labour market was seen as stable and close to maximum employment, though many saw signs of a modest tightening. A majority noted that financial conditions had tightened since the September meeting – as pointed out by Chair Kevin Warsh at the press conference – though several members believed that financial conditions remained supportive of growth. Economic activity was generally seen as strong, reflecting resilient household spending and robust investment.
Strong support for another rate increase in December, split thereafter
We view the minutes as strongly supportive of another rate increase in December, but with members more split about the path thereafter. The discussion in the October minutes is, however, outdated since it took place before recent stronger data for both the labour market (the higher-than-expected payroll growth in October) and for CPI inflation (which surprised on the upside in October and with relatively broad-based upside surprises). Recent comments from Fed members have in general been hawkish though Waller has been alone in discussing 50bp steps. 
We expect another rate increase in December and possibly also in March
FOMC members will not get much more data ahead of the December 8-9 FOMC meeting. There will be one more employment report, for November, released on 4 December, while November CPI will only be released the day after the FOMC meeting. Developments in financial conditions, including equities, and geopolitical developments in the Middle East, may also affect the decision. But barring any large surprises we expect the Fed to raise rates by another 25 bp at the December meeting. Members will also release new projections for the economy and rates, and we see it as likely that these will signal a large probability for at least one more rate increase in 2027, given that many members are now talking about further rate increases (in plural), though most seem to prefer a gradual pace rather than a larger 50 bp move. We continue to expect the Fed to raise rates again in December and possibly also in March 2027. Markets continue to price a small probability of a larger increase in December (27 bp) and at least two more rate increases until summer (81 bp by September).

articles.title: Nvidia beats expectations - Fed minutes tonight
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
Stock market indices in both Europe and the U.S. continued to decline yesterday, with the tech sector under pressure and new concerns about cybersecurity emerging after 
CNN reported
 network problems at the U.S. National Security Agency (NSA). The Euro Stoxx fell just over 2 percent and the S&P 500 by 1 percent, while long-term yields edged lower. The dollar weakened slightly against several other major currencies, but the Swedish krona fared worse, losing ground against all other G10 currencies. Nvidia’s after-close quarterly report yesterday 
beat expectations
, forecasting a revenue growth of 75 percent in 2028, which appears to be easing some of the concerns surrounding the AI sector for the time being. Asian stock markets are rising this morning, and futures point to a slightly positive opening in the U.S. and a flat opening in Europe. 
Today:
 A slew of central bank speeches are on today's agenda, including remarks by the ECB’s Lagarde and the Riksbank’s Hjelm, as well as UK inflation data and the Fed minutes tonight. Geopolitics is also likely to draw attention as Trump, Xi, and Putin, among others, gather at the APEC meeting in Shenzhen. The focus will be particularly on trade policy, AI, and geopolitical relations between the U.S. and China.
Fed minutes are in the spotlight tonight
. Incoming data continues to signal a resilient U.S. economy with elevated inflationary pressures, and the market is pricing in nearly 80 basis points higher policy rates by September of next year - almost 40 basis points more than just two weeks ago. Higher energy prices have slowed the decline in overall inflation and increased the risk of indirect effects through, for example, transportation costs. We see some signs that goods inflation is on the rise, while high mortgage rates are creating barriers in the housing market and risk leading to larger rent increases. While wage inflation continues to moderate, uncertainty surrounding the inflation outlook has increased and is putting pressure on the Fed.
UK core inflation is expected to ease slightly. 
The Bank of England raised its inflation forecast markedly at its most recent meeting, driven mainly by direct and indirect effects of high energy prices. We do not see support for such a sharp rise in short-term indicators and believe that the BoE is overestimating inflationary pressures going forward. Since the last meeting, the market has priced in a significantly tighter monetary policy over the coming year. 
While the risks are certainly on the upside for 
our forecast
 of a final interest rate hike in February, we also believe that the market is anticipating an overly aggressive tightening.
Nordic key stories
Swedish government negotiations continue
. After the Centre Party decided to move forward with the Social Democrats’ government government alternative, the deadlock over the Left Party’s demands for cabinet posts remains, and a final solution does not appear to be within reach. The exploratory talks are now on hold for a week to give the parties room for further negotiations, and all parties will then be summoned to a new round of talks with the Speaker next week. For the market, direct effects are very limited, but uncertainty surrounding economic policy remains. The Speaker said yesterday that he expects either a government or a new, extraordinary election to be announced before Christmas and New Year’s.
